pass_a_gloss: [...] earth the death through one, and the life to have no portion of good strength; for much more those having the grace through Christ and the gift of the righteousness out of the generosity from above will shake off the might of the death, and will reign together with the Christ who makes all things alive. So then, as through one trespass into all men into condemnation, and the rest. The divine Paul brings on to the thoughts set before, as it were, the conclusion, and says: So then, as through one trespass, and the following. For we have been condemned, as I said before, in Adam, and as from the first root the death from curse, having come about, went across into all that is from it; but we have been justified and have sprouted up again into life, Christ having been justified on our behalf. For the forefather, having been unsparing of the commandment given to him, struck against God and has endured the things from divine wrath; for he slid down into corruption; then also sin drove into the nature of man; so also the many were set down sinners, that is, those throughout all the earth. But someone might say: Yes, Adam slipped aside, and, having been heedless of the divine commandment, he was being condemned to corruption and death; then how were the many set down sinners through him? What [are] his stumblings toward us? And how at all have we, not yet born, been condemned with him? And yet God saying: Fathers will not die on behalf of children, nor children on behalf of fathers; the soul that sins, this one will die; what then would be the manner of the defence toward us? Therefore the soul that sins, this one will die; but we have become sinners through the disobedience of Adam through such a manner: for he had been made for incorruption and life, and his life too was holy-befitting in the paradise of the luxury; and the mind was whole and through all in God-seeings, and the body in fair weather and calm, every shameful pleasure being still; for there was no tumult of out-of-place movements in him; but since he has fallen under sin and slid down into corruption, from here pleasures and impurities ran into the nature of the flesh, and the law growing savage in our members sprang up. So the nature has been sick with the sin through the disobedience of the one, that is Adam; so the many were set down sinners, not as having transgressed together with Adam, for they were not ever [then], but as being of his nature, which fell under the law of the sin. Just as then the nature of man was sick with the corruption in Adam through the disobedience, and so the passions slipped into it, so it has been released again in Christ; for he became obedient to the God and Father, and did not do sin. But law came in beside, so that the trespass might increase. Someone will reason, he says, according to the likely, that thing somewhere, and says: Adam was a type of the one about to [come], and as in that one we were set down sinners through the transgression, so in Christ we have been justified through obedience. It was necessary, then, he says, for the justification in Christ to shine forth to those on earth with nothing taking up the middle.
pass_b_english: …earth, while life had no share of strength. For much more will those who have the grace that comes through Christ and the gift of righteousness from the bounty above shake off the power of death and reign together with Christ, who gives life to all things (Romans 5:17).

“Therefore, as through one trespass there came condemnation for all people,” and so on (Romans 5:18). To the thoughts already set out the inspired Paul adds, as it were, the conclusion, saying, “Therefore, as through one trespass,” and what follows. For we were condemned in Adam, as I said before, and death, which came from the curse, passed as from the first root into all that sprang from it. But we have been justified and have sprouted again into life, since Christ was justified on our behalf. For our forefather disregarded the commandment given to him, offended God, and underwent what comes from divine wrath, for he slid into corruption. Then sin also burst into human nature; and so the many were made sinners (Romans 5:19), that is, those throughout the whole earth.

But someone might say: Yes, Adam slipped, and because he disregarded the divine commandment he was condemned to corruption and death. But then how were the many made sinners because of him? What are his failings to us? And how at all were we, who had not yet been born, condemned along with him? And this although God says, “Fathers shall not die for their children” (Deuteronomy 24:16), nor children for their fathers; “the soul that sins, it shall die” (Ezekiel 18:20). What, then, would be the way of our defence? Certainly, “the soul that sins, it shall die”; but we became sinners through Adam's disobedience in the following way.

He had been made for incorruption and life, and in the paradise of delight he lived a life fit for the holy. His mind was wholly and constantly taken up with the vision of God, and his body was in calm and stillness, with every shameful pleasure at rest, for there was no tumult of unruly impulses in him. But when he fell under sin and slid into corruption, from then on pleasures and impurities rushed into the nature of the flesh, and the law that rages in our members sprang up (Romans 7:23). So nature caught the sickness of sin through the disobedience of the one, that is, Adam. In this way the many were made sinners (Romans 5:19): not as having transgressed together with Adam, for they did not yet exist at all, but as being of his nature, which fell under the law of sin.

Just as, then, human nature fell sick with corruption in Adam through disobedience, and so the passions slipped into it, so it has been set free again in Christ; for he became obedient to God the Father (Philippians 2:8) and committed no sin (1 Peter 2:22).

“The law came in, so that the trespass might increase” (Romans 5:20). Someone, he says, will reasonably argue along these lines and say: Adam “was a type of the one to come” (Romans 5:14), and just as we were made sinners in him through the transgression, so in Christ we have been justified through obedience. Then, he says, the justification in Christ should have appeared to those on earth with nothing coming in between.

γῆς τὸν δι' ἑνὸς θάνατον, εὐσθενείας γεμὴν ἀμοιρῆσαι τὴν ζωήν· πολλῷ γὰρ μᾶλλον οἱ
χάριν ἔχοντες τὴν διὰ Χριστοῦ καὶ τὴν τῆς δικαιοσύνης δωρεὰν ἐκ φιλοτιμίας τῆς
ἄνωθεν, ἀποσείσονται μὲν τοῦ θανάτου τὸ κράτος, συμβασιλεύσουσι δὲ τῷ ζωοποιοῦντι
τὰ πάντα Χριστῷ. 186 Ἄρα οὖν ὡς δι' ἑνὸς παραπτώματος εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους εἰς
κατάκριμα κ.τ.λ. Προσεπάγει ταῖς προκειμέναις ἐννοίαις ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος οἱονεὶ τὸ
συμπέρασμα καί φησιν Ἄρα οὖν ὡς δι' ἑνὸς παραπτώματος καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. κατακεκρίμεθα
μὲν γὰρ, ὡς προεῖπον, ἐν Ἀδὰμ, καὶ ὡς ἐκ ῥίζης τῆς πρώτης εἰς ἅπαν διέβη τὸ ἐξ αὐτῆς,
γενόμενος ὁ ἐξ ἀρᾶς θάνατος· δεδικαιώμεθα δὲ καὶ ἀνεβλαστήσαμεν εἰς ζωὴν,
δικαιωθέντος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τοῦ Χριστοῦ. ἀφειδήσας μὲν γὰρ τῆς αὐτῷ δοθείσης ἐντολῆς ὁ
προπάτωρ, προσκέκρουκε τῷ Θεῷ καὶ ὑπομεμένηκε τὰ ἐκ θείας ὀργῆς· κατώλισθε γὰρ
εἰς φθοράν· τότε καὶ εἰσήλατο τὴν ἀνθρώπου φύσιν ἡ ἁμαρτία· οὕτω καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ
κατεστάθησαν οἱ πολλοὶ, τουτέστιν οἱ ἀνὰ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν. Ἀλλ' εἴποι τις ἄν Ναὶ
παρώλισθεν ὁ Ἀδὰμ, καὶ τῆς θείας ἀλογήσας ἐντολῆς, φθορᾷ καὶ θανάτῳ κατεδικάζετο·
εἶτα πῶς ἁμαρτωλοὶ δι' αὐτὸν κατεστάθησαν οἱ πολλοί; τί πρὸς ἡμᾶς τὰ ἐκείνου
πταίσματα; πῶς δὲ ὅλως οἱ μήπω γεγενημένοι καταδεδικάσμεθα σὺν αὐτῷ; καίτοι Θεοῦ
λέγοντος "Οὐκ ἀποθανοῦνται πατέρες ὑπὲρ τέκνων," οὔτε τέκνα ὑπὲρ πατέρων, "ψυχὴ
ἡ ἁμαρτάνουσα αὕτη ἀποθανεῖται·" τίς οὖν ἂν γένοιτο πρὸς ἡμᾶς τῆς ἀπολογίας ὁ
τρόπος; οὐκοῦν ψυχὴ μὲν ἡ ἁμαρτάνουσα αὕτη ἀποθανεῖται· ἁμαρτωλοὶ δὲ γεγόναμεν
διὰ τῆς παρακοῆς τοῦ Ἀδὰμ διὰ τοιόνδε τρόπον· πεποίητο μὲν γὰρ ἐπὶ ἀφθαρσίᾳ καὶ
ζωῇ, ἦν δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ ὁ βίος ἁγιοπρεπὴς ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ τῆς τρυφῆς, ὅλος ἦν καὶ διὰ
παντὸς ἐν θεοπτίαις ὁ νοῦς, ἐν εὐδίᾳ δὲ καὶ γαλήνῃ τὸ σῶμα, κατηρεμούσης ἁπάσης
αἰσχρᾶς ἡδονῆς· οὐ γὰρ ἦν ἐκτόπων κινημάτων θόρυβος ἐν αὐτῷ· ἐπειδὴ δὲ πέπτωκεν

5

ὑφ' ἁμαρτίαν, καὶ κατώλισθεν εἰς φθορὰν, ἐντεῦθεν εἰσέδραμον τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς φύσιν
ἡδοναί τε καὶ ἀκαθαρσίαι, ἀνέφυ δὲ καὶ ὁ ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ἡμῶν ἀγριαίνων 187 νόμος.
νενόσηκεν οὖν ἡ φύσις τὴν ἁμαρτίαν διὰ τῆς παρακοῆς τοῦ ἑνὸς, τουτέστιν Ἀδάμ·
οὕτως ἁμαρτωλοὶ κατεστάθησαν οἱ πολλοὶ, οὐχ ὡς τῷ Ἀδὰμ συμπαραβεβηκότες, οὐ γὰρ
ἦσαν πώποτε, ἀλλ' ὡς τῆς ἐκείνου φύσεως ὄντες τῆς ὑπὸ νόμον πεσούσης τὸν τῆς
ἁμαρτίας. ὥσπερ τοίνυν ἠῤῥώστησεν ἡ ἀνθρώπου φύσις ἐν Ἀδὰμ διὰ τῆς παρακοῆς τὴν
φθορὰν, εἰσέδυ τε οὕτως αὐτὴν τὰ πάθη, οὕτως ἀπήλλακται πάλιν ἐν Χριστῷ· γέγονε
γὰρ ὑπήκοος τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ, καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησεν ἁμαρτίαν. Νόμος δὲ παρεισῆλθεν, ἵνα
πλεονάσῃ τὸ παράπτωμα. ∆ιαλογιεῖταί τις, φησὶ, κατὰ τὸ εἰκὸς ἐκεῖνό που καὶ λέγει
"Τύπος ἦν τοῦ μέλλοντος" ὁ Ἀδὰμ, καὶ ὥσπερ ἐν ἐκείνῳ κατεστάθημεν ἁμαρτωλοὶ διὰ
τὴν παράβασιν, οὕτως ἐν Χριστῷ δεδικαιώμεθα δι' ὑπακοῆς. ἔδει τοίνυν
μεσολαβοῦντος, φησὶν, οὐδενὸς τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ δικαίωσιν τοῖς ἐπὶ γῆς ἀναφαίνεσθαι·

revisions.summary: Pass A, lemmas, choices and bible_refs rebuilt from the Greek to match the reviewed English; pass_b_english is the current English.

review_notes: Old draft was a loose paraphrase with serious errors: 'the earth, full of strength, shares in life' for the end of the sentence that denies life a share of strength; 'remaining under divine wrath' for 'underwent what comes from divine wrath'; 'the nature of the flesh entered' where pleasures and impurities rushed into the nature of the flesh; 'law of the savage elements' for 'the law that rages in our members'; it dropped the Romans 5:18 lemma and Cyril's statement that Paul draws the conclusion, the root image, the objector's 'Yes, Adam slipped', the 'Certainly, the soul that sins' answer, the paradise description details, and the Romans 5:14 objection; it merged the Romans 5:20 lemma with the objection and inverted it into Cyril's own claim; cited only Ezekiel 18:20 for a quotation whose first clause is Deuteronomy 24:16; and the title 'Original Sin' imposes a later Western term. Retranslated in full, clause by clause. Scripture identified: Romans 5:17, 5:18, 5:19 (twice), 5:20, 5:14; Deuteronomy 24:16 (LXX οὐκ ἀποθανοῦνται πατέρες ὑπὲρ τέκνων); Ezekiel 18:20 (ψυχὴ ἡ ἁμαρτάνουσα αὕτη ἀποθανεῖται, also 18:4); Romans 7:23 (law in the members); Philippians 2:8 (γενόμενος ὑπήκοος); 1 Peter 2:22 (οὐκ ἐποίησεν ἁμαρτίαν). Column numbers 186-187 and page number 5 dropped. Opens mid-sentence (γῆς) from u02-rem-early; the objector's question continues at the start of u02-rem-close.
